transcript:
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Rylan Barton.
At a hearing today, a federal judge appeared inclined to order the White House to restore,
at least temporarily, the press passes of journalists for CNN, MS Now, and Politico.
U.S. District Court Judge Timothy Kelly said that, according to precedent, it was clear
that President Trump violated the news outlet's constitutional right of due process when it
banned their journalists from the White House.
The Justice Department has argued that precedent should be overturned, but Kelly said it was
not for him, as a district court judge, to do.
Iran's President Masoud Pizeshkin says his people have been victims of terrorism by the
U.S.
Iran must be understood by Mr. Trump and those who seek to bully us that we are ready for
dialogue and diplomacy and negotiations without accepting the language of force.
It was a rare wartime speech at the U.N. General Assembly a day after President Trump said
he could annihilate Iran.
He held up photos of the late Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei and the more than 150 school
children killed in the first days of the war.
He said that Iran's people have only defended themselves.
Chinese leader Xi Jinping will arrive in Washington, D.C. soon.
President Trump will personally greet him at Joint Base Andrews later today, and appears
Emily Feng reports on the pageantry the White House is planning for the Chinese president.
The U.S. military will conduct a flyover at the White House shortly before Trump meets
the Chinese leader on the tarmac tonight, showing just how important Trump sees this
visit.
On Thursday, the Marine Band will welcome the Chinese leader with the anthems of both countries
and a state visit reception with hundreds of U.S. military personnel and a gun salute,
as well as another flyover with fighter planes.
In addition to the pomp, the two leaders are expected to talk about trade, the war in Iran,
and artificial intelligence.
Activists also want Trump to raise the issue of detained Americans and dissidents in China.
And then Trump and Xi will gather for a state dinner, pared back in part due to Trump's
East Wing construction project.
Emily Feng, NPR News, the White House.
The latest NPR/PBS News/Marist poll looks at how President Trump is faring with voters
ahead of the midterms, and PR's Stephen Fowler has more on the findings.
Earlier this month at the Republican Party's midterm convention, Trump said to pretend
that he was on the ballot.
Many voters seem to have taken that insistence to heart, just maybe not in the way he's
hoping.
Over 33 percent of registered voters say they'd back a Democrat in congressional races.
A majority of those folks say that vote signals opposition to Trump.
And a large number of Republicans, including two in five who backed Trump in 2024, say
he is not much of a factor in their vote.
In another warning sign for Republicans, more people say they want to vote for candidates
bringing new ideas and change instead of experience and a proven record.
Stephen Fowler, NPR News.
Other U.S. stock indexes sank today after a report said both activity and costs for
U.S. businesses are rising at the fastest pace in years.
The S&P 500 slid three quarters of a percent.
This is NPR.
President Trump's Board of Peace is proposing a six-month, $2.45 billion plan to begin reconstruction
and governance in Gaza as a ceasefire struggles to stay afloat.
At a meeting of the group's board today, the governors unveiled a 66-point project blueprint
to get things started while acknowledging enormous hurdles must still be overcome.
The Israeli military has expanded its control of Gaza and occupies 60 percent of the territory.
Hamas has not given up its weapons.
Nearly 3,500 evangelical leaders have signed on to a letter asking the Trump administration
to once again allow refugee resettlement in the U.S.
NPR's Jason DeRose reports the programs often help those fleeing religious persecution.
The global Christian humanitarian organization World Relief helped organize the letter.
It says the American commitment to international religious freedom has been a hallmark of foreign
policy for decades and that one of the primary ways the U.S. has stood for religious liberty
has been to offer refuge to those persecuted for their faith.
Prior to the end of such programs during the second Trump administration, the U.S. resettled
roughly 80,000 people each year.
Polls of evangelical Christians, both laity and clergy, show strong support for the programs,
saying the U.S. has a moral responsibility to take in refugees.
Jason DeRose, NPR News.
With just a few days left in the Major League Baseball regular season, the American League
West division might make a particularly mediocre kind of history.
After yesterday's games, the Texas Rangers and Houston Astros are tied for first place,
both with losing records, 78 and 79.
No full-season division champion has ever had a losing record.
This is NPR News.
